storm.summary_layperson: No storms anywhere nearby — just a clear, chilly evening, with a frost advisory for inland areas tonight.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No marine-layer buffer in play: the air (57°F) is already cooler than the Sound (61°F) and the gap only widens as it cools to ~52°F by 7 PM.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: KOKX radar shows no precipitation echoes in range, there is no instability in the atmosphere (CAPE 0 J/kg), and NWS has no thunderstorm watches or warnings out. High pressure (about 1027 hPa) is in control with dry, cool northerly flow across the region. The only active alert is a Frost Advisory from NWS Upton running overnight into Saturday morning — a cold-night story, not a storm story.

Local modifier: none. The Sound’s protective effect works when warm air sits over cooler water, creating a stable layer that chokes storms. Today it’s the reverse — the Sound is 61°F and the air is 57°F, so there’s no stable layer at all. The air keeps cooling after the 6:01 PM sunset (to about 52°F by 7 PM) while the water holds its temperature, so the gap only moves further the wrong way through the evening.

Upper winds: there is moderate wind shear aloft (about 34 kt from the northwest), but with zero instability there is nothing for it to organize. It doesn’t change the call.

Most likely outcome: dry, clear, and quiet for the cove and surrounding towns alike through the evening and overnight. Temperatures fall quickly after sunset; inland spots may see frost by morning, while the shoreline stays a few degrees milder thanks to the warmer water.

What would change the call: nothing realistic in this window. A new storm risk would need moisture and instability returning, which no model guidance shows tonight.

wind.regime_label: Light gradient wind — no sea breeze, direction may wander
wind.tactics_blurb: A fading 5-knot southerly at the start goes light and variable by sunset — stay center, keep your head out of the boat for puffs, and don’t bank on any one side.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Regime: light gradient wind — no sea breeze in play. A sea breeze needs the land to be warmer than the water; today the air–water temperature difference is −4.1°F (air colder than the 61°F Sound), so there is no thermal engine. Background wind across the region averages only about 7 kt at the airport stations, and stations are split on direction (agreement 0.5) — classic light, wandering conditions.

What the cove is doing now: the Riverside YC station reads SSW 7 kt, gusting 10 (10-minute average 8 kt), and Bridgeport shows S 9 kt — a local southerly along the Connecticut shore. Most other stations, including Westchester and the eastern Sound, are northerly. The cove reading is more than 45° off the regional median (N), which points to a local eddy or shoreline effect rather than a true regional flow. We trust the club station for the cove, but this kind of local breeze has little behind it.

Through the window: expect the southerly to soften from about 5 kt at 17:00 to 3 kt around the 6:01 PM sunset, then go light and variable as the evening air cools and the surface layer goes calm under clear skies. HRRR has light ESE at 2–4 kt through 7 PM and fading; after that it’s near calm, possibly a faint northerly drift off the land as the shore cools below the water temperature.

⚠️ HRRR/obs divergence: the model says ESE (123°) while nearby western-Sound stations are averaging W (259°) and RYC is SSW (203°). With winds this light, direction will be set by whatever puff arrives rather than any steady flow — treat the direction column as a rough guide.

Fleet impact: 17:00 is the only usable breeze; by 18:00 it’s marginal (under 5 kt) and after that it’s drifter territory. If there’s racing, get it in early. Stay near the middle of the course, sail for pressure you can see on the water, and keep the boat moving through the lulls. Dress warm — temperatures drop into the low 50s after dark.
